title: Harden the MiniJsonReader JSON grammar with a dedicated reader test fixture
description:
## Summary
The 2026-09-06 next-slice audit (creaturecreator-next-slice-audit-26-09-06-16-00-00.md) found the MiniJsonReader DNA JSON parser accepts input that is not strict JSON, which can silently corrupt or mis-parse authored DNA. No dedicated MiniJsonReaderTests fixture exists.

## Scope
Harden `Runtime/Definition/MiniJsonReader.cs` grammar at the parser level (not in DefinitionValidator):
- F-303 (P1): Duplicate object member names silently last-write-wins (`MiniJsonReader.cs:102`, `result[key]=value`). Reject duplicate keys with DnaDeserializationException.
- F-304 (P2): Raw control characters (< 0x20) accepted inside strings (`MiniJsonReader.cs:194`). Reject them.
- F-305 (P2): Number grammar is looser than documented (`MiniJsonReader.cs:204,208` broad scan + double.TryParse). Implement strict `-? int frac? exp?` grammar, keep invariant conversion.
- F-310: Add a pure `MiniJsonReaderTests` grammar fixture (duplicate key, control char/newline/tab/NUL, numeric grammar, escaped strings). Keep `JsonDnaSerializerTests` focused on DNA semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Duplicate JSON object keys produce a deterministic deserialization error (no last-write-wins) with a focused test.
- Control chars inside strings are rejected; valid escapes still parse.
- Strict JSON number grammar is enforced; invalid numbers rejected.
- A `MiniJsonReaderTests` fixture covers the grammar boundaries above and passes in EditMode/play runtime.

## Validation
Focused EditMode/pure reader unit tests (no Unity scene required); dotnet Tests build clean.

## Findings
Confirmed at HEAD d3c7f12e. No existing MemorySmith task owns parser grammar (TSK-0126 IDnaSerializer seam and TSK-0088 DisplayName are Done and unrelated). See docs/audits/creaturecreator-audit-synthesis-2026-09-06-batch.md.

## Blockers
None.

## Next Step
Implement parser rejection rules and the reader test fixture; run focused tests.

comments.body:
## Implementation (worktree, uncommitted)
Hardened parser-level grammar in `Assets/Scripts/Runtime/Serialization/MiniJsonReader.cs` only (no DefinitionValidator/DNA-semantics change):
- F-303: ParseObject rejects duplicate member names via `result.ContainsKey(key)` -> throws `DnaDeserializationException("Duplicate JSON object member '<key>' at position <i>.")` then `result.Add`. Memory stays bounded by the object's own member count (Dictionary already holds first value; ContainsKey adds no storage); deterministic — always throws on second occurrence.
- F-304: ParseString rejects raw control chars (c < 0x20) in the non-escape path with `Unescaped control character (U+XXXX) ...`. Escaped forms (\n \t \" \\ \/ \b \f \r \uXXXX) still decode via the existing escape branch (unchanged).
- F-305: ParseNumber rewritten to strict JSON `-? int frac? exp?`: optional `-` only (no leading `+`); integer part `0` or non-zero digit+d; leading-zero rejection (`01`,`-01`,`00`); frac requires `.` + one+ ASCII digit; exponent `e`/`E` + optional sign + one+ digit; rejects hex/NaN/Infinity/trailing junk. Added ASCII-only digit helper (char.IsDigit would accept non-ASCII digits). Added post-conversion guard rejecting exponent overflow to +/-Infinity (`1e999`). Conversion stays invariant (`double.TryParse(token, NumberStyles.Float, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`).

Added pure grammar fixture `Assets/Scripts/Tests/Runtime/MiniJsonReaderTests.cs` (49 cases): duplicate keys (top/nested/type-change/deterministic message), raw control chars (newline/tab/CR/NUL/0x01/0x02/object value), valid escapes decode (\n,\t,",\,/,b,f,r,\uXXXX), and numeric grammar (13 valid forms + 18 invalid forms + overflow + trailing-junk + in-object). JsonDnaSerializerTests left untouched (still DNA-semantics only).

## Validation (real Unity, PlayMode)
Note: `ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime` assembly tests are discovered under PlayMode in this project (EditMode filter returned 0 tests), so the pure-reader fixture ran in PlayMode as the repo's runtime suite does — no scene dependency (fixture is plain [Test], no [UnityTest]/scene).
- Gate 1: `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Tests.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` -> exit 0 (Runtime + Tests.Runtime succeed); explicit `dotnet build ProceduralCreature.Runtime.csproj --no-restore` -> exit 0.
- Gate 2a: `MiniJsonReaderTests` PlayMode -> 49 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.
- Gate 2b: `JsonDnaSerializerTests` PlayMode -> 11 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (round-trip, byte-stability, legacy migration preserved => strict grammar accepts all CanonicalJsonWriter output: fixed-point `F4`/default `G` invariant forms, `-?` minus only, no leading zero/exponent).
- Gate 3: `git diff --check` -> exit 0 (no whitespace errors).
No console errors after compile.

## Non-obvious decisions
1) Duplicate keys: reject with `ContainsKey` then `Add` (bounded memory, deterministic second-occurrence throw, names the key). Not using `Dictionary.Add`'s raw ArgumentException so the message is stable and the outer Parse wrapper doesn't mask it with a generic "Malformed JSON near position" wrap.
2) Number grammar edge handling: ASCII-only digits (not char.IsDigit); leading-zero integer rule follows JSON (`0` ok, `01` bad); fraction/exponent require at least one digit; a leading `+` and bare `.5`/`1.` are rejected; exponent overflow to +/-Infinity rejected as non-finite (digits can't spell NaN/Infinity literally, but `1e999` can overflow).
3) Preserving existing valid DNAs: CanonicalJsonWriter only emits invariant `-?` fixed-point/`G` numbers (e.g. `0.7500`, `-0.2500`, `2`) — all strict-grammar valid, confirmed by 11/11 JsonDnaSerializerTests including byte-stable round-trip. No authored file should rely on leading `+`, leading zeros, hex, or raw control chars; such inputs were previously mis-parsed and are the defect being fixed.

## Residual risk
- The `1e999` overflow rejection is a deliberate strictness beyond "loose grammar" (documented) — an extreme but finite-looking exponent now errors instead of silently producing Infinity. No valid DNA uses it.
- Control-char rejection also applies to any human-authored JSON that embedded a literal newline inside a string (invalid JSON); such files now fail at load rather than mis-parse.

## Next step
Orchestrator review of the working-tree diff (uncommitted, per round rules).
